observations.body: The discourse remembers the mother and seven sons, describes their contest before the tyrant, and contrasts the tyrant’s punishment with the brothers’ enduring life and honor before God.

payload.posture: Read 4 Maccabees 17:7–18 as one movement in the resurrection, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states the discourse remembers the mother and seven sons, describes their contest before the tyrant, and contrasts the tyrant’s punishment with the brothers’ enduring life and honor before God. It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of the resurrection.
payload.title: Martyrdom is remembered through immortality and enduring life
